pbtfans-absolute.description: PBTfans Absolute draws inspiration from Kazimir Malevich's Suprematist art movement. The set features a warm beige base color (GMK L9) that serves as a canvas for geometric compositions that follow Suprematism's principle of alogism: geometric shapes overlapping without strict hierarchy, colors combining without seeking conventional harmony, and elements floating freely in space. These compositions do not carry symbolic meaning: they exist as pure visual form. That's why this keycap set isn't meant to have any deeper meaning, but is simply there to be appreciated visually. — PBTfans AbsoluteDye subPBTfans

pbtfans-spark-3.description: Finding Balance: The Story Behind the very first PBTfans keycap set.  This keycap set is built around the concept of balance, starting with a simple, clean foundation and giving you the choice to add colorful personality where you want it. I wanted to create something special for the very first PBTfans set, so I focused on the idea that simple doesn't have to mean boring. — PBTfans Spark3InjectionPBTfans

kc-orange.description: kc_orange: Capturing the essence of Orange Box's iconic development maps, where orange walls and grey textures became iconic.  kc_orange is deeply personal to me. I spent countless hours on those iconic orange development maps. Whether it was grinding aim training on aim_ag_texture2 in Counter-Strike Source or running endless rounds on 3xi_trainmap (mostly on the "Worst Case Scenario" server) in Day of Defeat Source, these orange environments became my second home. When I designed these keycaps, I wanted each one to feel like a box model with defined edges and strokes, just like those geometric textures that made up every surface in those maps.  I chose to base the orange modifier keys on the warm tones that covered the walls and barriers of maps such as orange_x3 and countless other community creations. The colours draw inspiration from the iconic orange and grey palettes that defined the Source engine aesthetic. My goal was to honour how these simple, repetitive textures became beautiful in their own way. Each keycap is designed with clean edge strokes that mirror the box modelling approach used in those environments. There's something mesmerising about those orange surfaces stretching infinitely, broken only by the geometric patterns of grey infrastructure.  What fascinated me most about these maps was their accidental poetry. I wanted to capture the strange beauty of these liminal gaming spaces through the architectural quality of each keycap. These environments weren't trying to be realistic or impressive; they were simply functional geometric shapes that made the map easy to remember and created a focus on the gameplay.  The novelties (keycaps) feature special designs such as 'Capsule 3' branding, references to the minimap, and symbols nodding to Half-Life 2 and other beloved Source games. I decided that these white accents were essential because they serve as little Easter eggs for fellow gamers who lived through that era — just as small details became focal points.  These keycaps are about more than just nostalgia. They're about recognising the unexpected beauty in utilitarian design and translating three-dimensional thinking into something tangible. Whenever I see this set, I'm reminded that the most compelling spaces are often those that aren't trying to be anything other than themselves. The orange maps taught us that beauty can exist in repetition and simplicity, as well as in the spaces between things.  This is my tribute to the imperfections that shaped how we see digital environments, now rendered as tangible box models that you can touch. — kc_orangeDye subKeyreative

pbtfans-twist.description: Born from a desire to pay tribute to the first home computers such as the Thomson TO7 or the Canon V20, this set has its roots in industrial design.   Once again, a neo-retro set that proves my obsession with old keyboards and microcomputers from the 1980s.   It's a vintage looking keyset that pays homage to its predecessors while remaining contemporary. Understated, go-anywhere, its grayscale color scheme matches any keyboard that's reminiscent of most keyboards seen in the 80s, as well as the yellow accent color which adds a touch of singularity. The triple-shot technology makes it possible to have a different legend color and sub legend color, adding a new touch of uniqueness, in addition to the extra top row with a lighter gray.  This is the third run of PBTfans Twist. — PBTfans Twist3InjectionPBTfans

pbtfans-spark-light-2.description: The Lighter Side of PBTfans Spark  This is the lighter interpretation of my Spark keycap set philosophy, where I switched the foundation from deep navy to a clean, soft gray base. The same concept of balance remains: starting with a simple base color but giving you optional colorful accents. My approach was to prove that the same design concept can work in completely different moods.  This is a rerun of PBTfans Spark light. — PBTfans Spark Light2InjectionPBTfans

pbtfans-virtuoso.description: Virtuoso keycaps translate synthesizer aesthetics into mechanical keyboard form.   The set draws from Teenage Engineering's design philosophy where electronic instruments become artistic tools. The restrained palette uses whites and grays as the foundation, with orange modifiers marking key functions and warm beige novelties referencing vintage analog gear. The music-inspired novelties feature custom icons representing elements of electronic music production, such as waveforms, oscillators, speakers, knobs, buttons and various symbols from the OP-1 Field, which also influenced the colour scheme of the keycap set. — PBTfans VirtuosoDye subPBTfans

pbtfans-confettis.description: Inspired by the natural scatter of confetti and the beauty of controlled randomness, this keycap set reflects a contemporary design philosophy that values both function and form.   The concept embraces the idea that workspaces can be both professional and personally expressive, offering a quiet way to bring individuality to your setup while maintaining the clean aesthetics that modern users appreciate.  Like finding confetti days after a celebration, these gentle splashes of color create a sense of discovered joy in your daily routine. — PBTfans ConfettisDye subPBTfans

pbtfans-no-signal.description: Inspired by the popular test patterns which were used to calibrate televisions, in particular, its colors and graphic elements.   When I was young, I stumbled upon a television channel that was showing a test pattern. I was immediately fascinated by its visual appearance, which was very colourful and high-contrast.  The concept is that the keyboard, once assembled, therefore becomes a calibration tool in turn. The graphic elements are inspired by direct references to different types of test patterns: The Indian-head test pattern, SMPTE color and undoubtedly the most famous and iconic of all the PTV Circle pattern. Initially the test cards were displayed when the television channel had not yet started its programs. Used as a signal, they can appear during unforeseen events: breakdowns, staff strike, signal cut, power cut, regional stall, etc... Those are now part of popular culture, although sometimes diverted from their original use, we can spot them in current productions such as Fallout 4 with its iconic test card (based on The RCA Indian-head test pattern) or Life on Mars with the use of the BBC Test card F. — PBTfans No Signal2Dye subPBTfans

pbtfans-nano.description: A Tribute to Computing Heritage, especially the iconic Thomson MO5NR, a French home computer that defined an era of personal computing.   I wanted to create something that felt both nostalgic and fresh (once again). The Thomson MO5NR had this unique charm with its distinctive color scheme, and I knew I had to translate that into a modern keycap set. My goal was to honor the original computer while making the colors work beautifully on today's keyboards. This set features a dedicated colour palette inspired by that computer, with warm cream, cool grey and striking blue and mint accents that capture the essence of computing aesthetics from that era. — PBTfans NanoDye subPBTfans

pc-neon-lights.description: Walking Through Neon Streets: The Inspiration Behind PC Neon Lights  PC Neon Lights is a keycap set that captures the vibrant energy of neon-lit cityscapes and gaming culture. The design features a sleek dark cold semi-opaque gray base with bright, colorful legends that seem to glow against the dark surface. — PC Neon LightsUV Print

It's a vintage looking keyset that pays homage to its predecessors while remaining contemporary. gmk-extended-2048.description: A tribute to the iconic Apple Extended Keyboard II from the early 1990s.  My idea was to offer a timeless looking keycap set that would never feel outdated. I wanted to create something with meaningful but easy to recognize legends (icons & alphas), the kind of symbols that feel intuitive and universal rather than trendy or complex, since that's also the DNA of the AEKII.  — GMK Extended 2048InjectionGMK electronic design

kat-operator.description: Smooth Operator: Designing keycaps with Industrial Inspiration and Modern Functionality.  For this set I designed a rounded, modernist font because it feels approachable while still maintaining the readability. One of the key features of this set is the dual-legend approach. Many keycaps display two functions or symbols, which I decided to implement for practical reasons. This allows the base kit to work with more keyboard layouts while keeping everything you need in one set.  The iconography throughout the set uses simple, recognizable symbols that maintain the utilitarian theme. I decided to keep decorative elements to a minimum, since the alphas were already kinda _busy_, focusing instead on making every visual choice serve a purpose.  _This is a rerun of the MT3 Operator keycap set from 2023._ — KAT OperatorInjectionKeyreative

kam-playground.description: Designing keycaps for everyone's unique workflow, from macro-pad users to content creators.  I always had the desire to offer a set that would be suitable for everyone, but beyond that, a set suitable for all uses. Most of the time, macro-pad and ortho users don't have well-designed keycap options for their specific needs. I wanted to solve this problem in a playful way while also serving MOBA/FPS players, music producers, and content creators. I decided to go with KAM's uniform profile because it offers more layout flexibility than sculpted profiles.  What makes this set special is how it adapts to different users. A streamer might highlight their recording and streaming controls, while a music producer could emphasize their audio software shortcuts. Gamers can mark their essential macros, and productivity users can identify their most-used applications at a glance. I chose to include such a wide variety of icons because I believe everyone's keyboard should reflect their unique workflow and personality. — KAM PlaygroundInjectionKeyreative

pbtfans-doppelganger.description: OG-Inspired Multilingual Keycaps  The Doppelganger serie ddresses the practical needs of multilingual users through its comprehensive legend system that supports multiple layouts on each key. This practical approach transforms the traditional challenge of offering multiple language support into a streamlined, budget-friendly solution.  I chose a vintage-inspired color scheme to provide a stable foundation for this linguistic abundance, while my consolidated approach means users can support multiple languages without investing in separate keycap sets. Like the namesake suggests, I designed each keycap to exist as multiple versions of itself, serving different layouts simultaneously. — PBTfans DoppelgangerDye subPBTfans

kat-white-on-black.description: Perfect balance between sobriety and playfulness.  Inspired by the iconography of retro synthesizers, the keycap set lets you juggle between the classic white-on-black style, which can be combined with any keyboard, and a colorful look for more singularity and uniqueness. In both cases, it's all about elegant subtlety. — KAT White on BlackInjectionKeyreative

boop65-redux.description: Introducing boop65 redux, a refined version of its predecessor.  A timeless design with seamless and fully rounded edges, once again but with an even sleeker design, improved compatibility and a new feature: the external LED indicator. — boop65 reduxInjection

gmk-nightlife.description: Inspired by the nocturnal atmosphere of Japanese streets, corroborated with neon signs. — GMK NightlifeInjectionGMK electronic design

kat-milkshake-double-shot.description: KAT Milkshake: Rounded typography & pastel colors capture classic milkshake drink vibes.  I chose KAT because the taller, rounder, smoother, sculpted shape of this profile reminds me of classic tall milkshake glasses. The curved tops of the KAT keycaps echo the rounded, bubbly foam that sits on top of a perfectly made milkshake, which makes this profile a natural fit for the theme.  I wanted to create something that felt both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. The name "Milkshake" came from that creamy, sweet feeling I was going for with the color palette. My goal was to design a set that would make people smile when they looked at their keyboard.  It is a playful keycap set that brings together soft pastels and colorful fruit-inspired accents. The base uses slightly warm off-white keycaps with rounded uppercase lineal dark legends that create excellent readability while maintaining a gentle, approachable look.  The keyset also features a custom handcrafted font called "Weirdos," which is based on a(ny) classic sans-serif rounded font but has had sections of the letters removed to create a unique, singular look. The result is a sci-fi but minimalistic looking font that perfectly matches the organic and playful modifiers icons. This addition further enhances the overall tone of the set, making it a truly one-of-a-kind keycaps set that is sure to stand out.  This is a rerun of 2019 dye sub KAT Milkshake. — KAT Milkshake Double shot2InjectionKeyreative

mt3-extended-2048-dark.description: Extending 2048 After Dark  If you’re going by military time, 20:48 is prime time. Work’s over, and the night’s just coming to life. That’s the moment we’re chasing on the new Drop + biip MT3 Extended 2048 Dark Keycap Set—a darkened take on a community favorite, and our first-ever reverse dye-sublimated set. Sporting black alphas where the original’s were cream-colored, Extended 2048 Dark earns its name with an after-dark vibe that still makes plenty of nods to its inspiration: the Apple Extended Keyboard II (AEKII). Like its predecessor—and like any true nightlife—it’s filled with a host of accent colors that add welcome levity to the dark. Look for them on select modifiers, where you’ll find standard dye-sublimated legends matching Apple’s unmistakable iconography. You’ll also find durable PBT construction with a distinctly reimagined retro feel—all courtesy of our scooped, sculpted, and ultra-satisfying MT3 profile. It’s an all-around typing throwback, Extended into the late night. It’s getting Dark. — MT3 Extended 2048 DarkDye sub

gmk-trackday.description: Smell the burning tires, smoking breaks, immerse yourself deep in the car scene with GMK Trackday.  GMK Trackday is a tribute to the public track racing events that take place all around the world and gather cars aficionados. — GMK TrackdayInjectionGMK electronic design

pbt-industrial-keys.description: Form Follows Function: An Industrial Design Study  This keycap set draws inspiration from the clean, functional design philosophy of legendary industrial designers like Charles Eames, Dieter Rams, and Jony Ive. The result is a minimalist approach that focuses on pure functionality and timeless aesthetics.  The standout feature is the bright orange accent system, which serves as both decoration and functional guidance. I decided to use this pop of color very strategically. Indeed, you can see it on the Shift key and also on the top legends of the number row keys (the symbols like !, @, #, etc.). My goal was to create a visual connection between the Shift key and the characters that require it to be pressed.  Overall, this set represents my attempt to bring the timeless principles of industrial design into the mechanical keyboard world: creating something that is both good looking (I hope) and practical, with no unnecessary elements to distract from its core purpose. — PBT Industrial KeysDye sub

pbt-raw.description: Bold forms and raw, uncompromising designs are the hallmarks of this Brutalist-inspired keycap set.  I believe that every creator/designer needs, at some point, to see how far they can go in their creative endeavours…  I wanted to embrace brutalist graphic design's love for bold, unapologetic visual expression. My goal was to turn the keyboard into a canvas (I would not call it art piece but this is the idea), something that demands attention and makes people stop and look. I chose this high-contrast blue and white palette because I wanted maximum visual impact, not subtlety. The decorative symbols aren't about functionality, but singular expression.  The set also includes a few hidden easter eggs for people who look closely. I decided to add these personal touches because even the most serious design movements had moments of playfulness.  — PBT RAWDye sub

pc-clear-2048.description: Exploring Smoky Transparency Inspired by Iconic 90s Tech Aesthetics  My idea was to offer something that celebrates the experimental spirit of 90s design while still feeling sophisticated today. I was inspired by iconic translucent products like the atomic purple Game Boy Color, translucent iMacs, and those amazing see-through Nintendo 64 controllers that showed off the internal components. There was something honest and exciting about being able to see inside your devices.  The translucent material adds a completely different character to the Extended 2048 design language. While the original versions focused on timeless minimalism, Clear 2048 embraces transparency as both a design element and a statement. — PC Clear 2048UV PrintPBTfans

wrk-cartridge.description: My utilitarian methodology behind timeless but industry inspired color choices and adaptable iconography that allows users to arrange keys based on personal habits.  Cartridge is a keycap set that draws inspiration from retro gaming aesthetics while maintaining a modern, clean approach to design. The set features a light gray foundation with strategic use of purple and orange accent colors that create visual hierarchy and functional distinction across the layout.  I wanted the typography to feel clean and readable, similar to the industrial approach I used in MT3 Operator. The legends maintain excellent contrast against both the light gray base and colored accent keys. I chose to keep the font treatment consistent across all keys to maintain visual unity.  The name "Cartridge" reflects both the gaming inspiration and the modular nature of keycap sets themselves. I liked the idea that keycaps are like cartridges you can swap in and out to change your keyboard's personality. — WRK CartridgeDye sub

gmk-parcel.description: If the hobby of mechanical keyboards teaches us one thing, it is patience.   But above all, it is a whole lexicon around the packages that we have to learn: Track, Dispatch, Ship, Deliver, etc.  I wanted to create something that felt familiar yet special, so I chose the postal theme because everyone can relate to sending and receiving packages.  — GMK ParcelInjectionGMK electronic design

pbt-notion.description: A playful and colorful A keycap set designed to be practical, while improving legends visibility and readability, allowing users to express their own style.  PBT Notion is a clean, minimalist keycap set built around a custom typeface I designed specifically for this project. The set features crisp white keycaps with deep blue legends and colorful optional accents. — PBT NotionDye sub

gmk-dots-2.description: When Less Becomes More: How I searched for the most minimalistic keycap legend possible.  Where do we draw the line between legends and novelties? The genesis of Dots was born from the desire of a unique and creative way to rethink keycap sets that depart from traditional/common letters and numbers.  My goal was to solve a real problem I noticed with blank keycaps. Yes, blank sets look clean and work with any language, but they're really hard to use if you can't touch-type perfectly. I thought: what if there was something in between? Something minimal but still helpful? That's how I came to the idea of dots (even though it was originally an April Fool's joke).  The dots (if we could call those dots) of the modifiers keycaps are coloured to visually guide the user, who is even free to place keycaps with coloured dots wherever they want on their keyboard as a reference point (for example, while learning to type on blank keyboards, I placed red dots on the number row so I could find the 5 and 0 at a glance).  Additionally, With dots instead of legends (or as legends), the set can accomplish the same functionality, covering any layout, with fewer keycaps and obviously a cheaper price.  This rerun introduced light version of GMK Dots. — GMK Dots2InjectionGMK electronic design

epbt-cool-kids-2.description: Another set, born yet again from an April Fool's Day prank (but is that really the case?).  It's a keycap set about joyful energy of kindergarten, through playful colors and randomly placed alphas. I wanted to capture that feeling where learning feels like play, surrounded by a gentle chaos. — EPBT Cool Kids2Dye subEnjoyPBT

gmk-awaken.description: Rooted in the aesthetics of futuristic technology and the electric atmosphere of cyberpunk narratives.  GMK Awaken features a dark base color paired with bright cyan and yellow legends, with some vibrant red accents, creating the classic cyberpunk color palette seen in sci-fi films and anime. I chose these colors because they evoke the feeling of glowing screens in dark environments and electronic displays coming to life.  The bilingual legends blend English (latin) legends with Japanese sub legends, reflecting the multicultural world often depicted in cyberpunk stories. I decided to design and include Japanese (Katakana) characters because they add authenticity to the futuristic theme while creating visual depth and international appeal. The Japanese characters aren't just decorative - it enhances the high-tech atmosphere that defines the genre.  Unique novelties replace standard modifiers with various sci-fi/circuit-inspired graphics and technological symbols. My goal was to transform these functional keys into artistic elements that reinforce the electronic theme. Yes, it's visually dense, but I think it perfectly captures the interfaces we saw in those 1980s action films. Indeed, I really wanted to create a design that captures the very essence of technological awakening through bold visual choices.  Awaken represents the moment when technology and consciousness merge: when systems boot up, displays illuminate, and digital worlds come alive. I designed this set for enthusiasts who appreciate cyberpunk culture, anime aesthetics, or anyone drawn to the visual language of our digital future. — GMK AwakenInjectionGMK electronic design

dsa-milkshake-2.description: DSA Milkshake: Rounded typography & pastel colors capture classic milkshake drink vibes. I wanted to create something that felt both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. The name "Milkshake" came from that creamy, sweet feeling I was going for with the color palette. My goal was to design a set that would make people smile when they looked at their keyboard.  It is a playful keycap set that brings together soft pastels and colorful fruit-inspired accents. The base uses slightly warm off-white keycaps with rounded uppercase lineal dark legends that create excellent readability while maintaining a gentle, approachable look.  The keyset also features a custom handcrafted font called "Weirdos," which is based on a(ny) classic sans-serif rounded font but has had sections of the letters removed to create a unique, singular look. The result is a sci-fi but minimalistic looking font that perfectly matches the organic and playful modifiers icons. This addition further enhances the overall tone of the set, making it a truly one-of-a-kind keycaps set that is sure to stand out. — DSA Milkshake2Dye sub

ec-extended-2048.description: A tribute to the iconic Apple Extended Keyboard II from the early 1990s.  This is the EC version of EPBT Extended 2048, designed to electro-capacitive keyboards.  My idea was to offer a timeless looking keycap set that would never feel outdated. I wanted to create something with meaningful but easy to recognize legends (icons & alphas), the kind of symbols that feel intuitive and universal rather than trendy or complex, since that's also the DNA of the AEKII. The set comes in two main colorways - a clean light version with cream-colored alphas and a sophisticated dark variant with deep charcoal keys. Both versions maintain the classic minimalist aesthetic that made the original Apple keyboard so memorable.  The legends use a custom typeface that I designed specifically for this project, carefully balancing readability with period-correct character. I wanted the font to feel familiar yet refined, just like the original. All the icons and symbols were also created from scratch to match the Apple aesthetic perfectly. This was particularly challenging because I had to consider the technical limitations of double-shot injection molding throughout the design process. Every curve and line weight was optimized to ensure clean, crisp production while maintaining the visual harmony of the set.  My goal was to create more than just a nostalgic keycap set. I wanted to design something that honors computing history while feeling completely at home on a modern mechanical keyboard. Extended 2048 bridges past and present, offering both vintage charm and contemporary functionality. — EC Extended 2048Dye sub

gmk-honor.description: A calmer and more subtle version of GMK Bushidō. — GMK HonorInjectionGMK electronic design

mt3-extended-2048.description: A Legendary Keyboard Lives On  When you bought an Apple Macintosh computer in the early 1990s, you received the Apple Extended Keyboard II (AEKII) along with it. While it may seem ordinary by modern standards, it was this very keyboard that would become a benchmark for future full-size boards—a legend of its time and still today. For our latest project, we teamed up with designer biip (who you may know from keycap sets like Milkshake, Bento, and Bushido) to create a set inspired by the legendary AEKII. Executed in our exclusive MT3 profile, our Extended 2048 keycap set features a minimal icons-based design with cream-colored alphas, black legends, and bright color accent keys. Made of PBT material with dye-sublimated construction, MT3 Extended 2048 is built strong with legends that won’t fade. — MT3 Extended 2048Dye sub

gmk-bento-2.description: Inspired by the Japanese culture, and the iconic/typical home-packed meal called 'Bento (弁当)  Creating GMK Bentō meant translating the philosophy behind Japanese bento culture into keyboard design. These aren't just lunch boxes, they're expressions of care, attention to detail, and aesthetic harmony that I wanted to capture.  The color scheme speaks to comfort and tradition. Warm cream used as base color evokes the rice that anchors every meal, the salmon red provides a pop of energy and liveliness, while deep teal blue draws from centuries of Japanese indigo craftsmanship. I believe colors should tell stories, and these hues whisper of home kitchens and careful hands preparing something special.  In addition to the color scheme, the set features minimalistic icons inspired by Japanese bento boxes.   The revival base kit was introduced in this second round. — GMK Bento2InjectionGMK electronic design

kam-wraith.description: Heavily inspired (and assumed) by the Sinclair ZX Spectrum from 1982, this set aims to have an 80s aesthetic with double colored legends, which is kinda unique and innovative IMO. This is possible using the all-over dye-sub technique.  The keycaps are labeled with the corresponding functions, just like on the original ZX Spectrum keyboard. These function keys were used to enter data, navigate the screen, and control the color of the text and graphics displayed on the screen. — KAM WraithDye subKeyreative

epbt-cool-kids.description: Another set, born yet again from an April Fool's Day prank (but is that really the case?).  It's a keycap set about joyful energy of kindergarten, through playful colors and randomly placed alphas. I wanted to capture that feeling where learning feels like play, surrounded by a gentle chaos. — EPBT Cool KidsDye subEnjoyPBT

gmk-bushido.description: GMK Bushidō is a dark-themed keycap set inspired by samurai culture and Japanese history. The design centers around a carefully balanced color scheme that combines cold gray and light gray tones with vivid red accents.  The keyset draws inspiration from samurai and Japanese historical themes, aiming to capture the essence of this cultural period through typography and color choices. The dark theme emphasizes the serious, disciplined nature associated with samurai culture. — GMK BushidoInjectionGMK electronic design

gmk-bento.description: Inspired by the Japanese culture, and the iconic/typical home-packed meal called 'Bento (弁当)  Creating GMK Bentō meant translating the philosophy behind Japanese bento culture into keyboard design. These aren't just lunch boxes, they're expressions of care, attention to detail, and aesthetic harmony that I wanted to capture.  The color scheme speaks to comfort and tradition. Warm cream used as base color evokes the rice that anchors every meal, the salmon red provides a pop of energy and liveliness, while deep teal blue draws from centuries of Japanese indigo craftsmanship. I believe colors should tell stories, and these hues whisper of home kitchens and careful hands preparing something special.  In addition to the color scheme, the set features minimalistic icons inspired by Japanese bento boxes.  — GMK BentoInjectionGMK electronic design

kat-milkshake.description: KAT Milkshake: Rounded typography & pastel colors capture classic milkshake drink vibes.  I chose KAT because the taller, rounder, smoother, sculpted shape of this profile reminds me of classic tall milkshake glasses. The curved tops of the KAT keycaps echo the rounded, bubbly foam that sits on top of a perfectly made milkshake, which makes this profile a natural fit for the theme.  I wanted to create something that felt both nostalgic and fresh at the same time. The name "Milkshake" came from that creamy, sweet feeling I was going for with the color palette. My goal was to design a set that would make people smile when they looked at their keyboard.  It is a playful keycap set that brings together soft pastels and colorful fruit-inspired accents. The base uses slightly warm off-white keycaps with rounded uppercase lineal dark legends that create excellent readability while maintaining a gentle, approachable look.  The keyset also features a custom handcrafted font called "Weirdos," which is based on a(ny) classic sans-serif rounded font but has had sections of the letters removed to create a unique, singular look. The result is a sci-fi but minimalistic looking font that perfectly matches the organic and playful modifiers icons. This addition further enhances the overall tone of the set, making it a truly one-of-a-kind keycaps set that is sure to stand out. — KAT Milkshake 1Dye subKeyreative

epbt-extended-2048.description: A tribute to the iconic Apple Extended Keyboard II from the early 1990s.  My idea was to offer a timeless looking keycap set that would never feel outdated. I wanted to create something with meaningful but easy to recognize legends (icons & alphas), the kind of symbols that feel intuitive and universal rather than trendy or complex, since that's also the DNA of the AEKII. The set comes in two main colorways - a clean light version with cream-colored alphas and a sophisticated dark variant with deep charcoal keys. Both versions maintain the classic minimalist aesthetic that made the original Apple keyboard so memorable.  The legends use a custom typeface that I designed specifically for this project, carefully balancing readability with period-correct character. I wanted the font to feel familiar yet refined, just like the original. All the icons and symbols were also created from scratch to match the Apple aesthetic perfectly. This was particularly challenging because I had to consider the technical limitations of double-shot injection molding throughout the design process. Every curve and line weight was optimized to ensure clean, crisp production while maintaining the visual harmony of the set.  My goal was to create more than just a nostalgic keycap set. I wanted to design something that honors computing history while feeling completely at home on a modern mechanical keyboard. Extended 2048 bridges past and present, offering both vintage charm and contemporary functionality. — EPBT Extended 2048Dye subEnjoyPBT
